answer: The help center names two forms as introduced on February 1, 2026. NW-POA-2 is the power of attorney that replaced NW-POA-1. It can be signed electronically without a notary, except in Georgia, where it must still be notarized. NW-ODO-2 is the odometer disclosure statement that replaced NW-ODO-1. Other forms appear in current articles (NW-MIL-1, NW-TRD-1, NW-LPA-1, NW-EST-1 and NW-DMG-1), but none is described as new since that date. The help center has no full change log, so it can't confirm the list is complete; please check with a store. Also note that the older article 'Selling a family member's car for them' still tells customers to use a notarized NW-POA-1, which is accepted only if it was signed before February 1, 2026 and only until June 30, 2026.
